# Datavzrd

> Datavzrd turns tabular data (CSV, TSV, JSON or Parquet) into interactive, self-contained HTML reports. Reports are described in a short YAML configuration and need no server, only a web browser.

Datavzrd is a command line tool written in Rust. It is installed via conda-forge (`conda install -c conda-forge datavzrd` or `pixi global install datavzrd`) and run as `datavzrd config.datavzrd.yaml --output report/`. A report consists of datasets (input tables) and views. Each view renders one dataset as a table (`render-table`), a Vega-Lite plot (`render-plot`), custom HTML and JavaScript (`render-html`) or an image (`render-img`). Columns of a table can be shown as heatmaps, tick, bar or bubble plots, pills, links to external resources or custom plots, and datasets can be linked to each other.

Things to keep in mind when writing a configuration:

- Only use keys that exist in the JSON schema below. Naming the file `*.datavzrd.yaml` lets editors with SchemaStore support validate it automatically.
- `datavzrd suggest -f data.csv -s ,` prints a working starting configuration for a given table.
- A `heatmap` needs either a `type`, or a `scale` together with a `color-scheme` or `range`.
- Custom JavaScript (e.g. `custom`, `custom-plot` data functions) is given as a function, usually `function(value, row)`.
- Header rows under `render-table: headers` are counted from 0 (the column names), so customizing row 1 requires `headers: 2` in the dataset.
- Column names within a dataset must be unique.

## Docs

- [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/installation.rst): Installing datavzrd with conda, pixi or cargo
- [Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/usage.rst): Command line arguments and the `suggest`, `schema` and `publish` subcommands
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/configuration.rst): Full reference of all configuration keys
- [Tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/tutorial.rst): Step by step introduction building a report from an Oscar winners dataset
- [Advanced tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/advanced_tutorial.rst): Templating configurations with YTE, linking views and using your own data
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/troubleshooting.rst): Common error messages and how to fix them
- [Spells](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/spells.rst): Reusable configuration snippets for common column types

## Reference

- [Configuration schema](https://datavzrd.github.io/schema/latest/datavzrd.schema.json): JSON schema of the configuration file, also printed by `datavzrd schema`
- [Example configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd/main/.examples/example.datavzrd.yaml): Configuration of the live demo report using most features
- [Live demo](https://datavzrd.github.io/datavzrd/oscars/index_1.html): A rendered example report

## Optional

- [Workflow integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datavzrd/datavzrd.github.io/main/src/docs/wms_integration.rst): Using datavzrd from Snakemake and Nextflow
